messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: High GPU provisioning queue growth detected in us-west-2. Autoscaler failing to register new GPU nodes (register timeout + taint propagation). ~1200 queued inference requests, multiple customer errors (503/timeout). Paging oncall.
Alyssa S.: I'm on it — looking at cluster-autoscaler logs now. Seeing a bunch of `register node` timeouts and `AttachRole` failures for the gpu-nodegroup.
Jay K.: Confirming: launch template version drift on the nodegroup -> instances boot with older kubelet config. They never complete `kubelet register`. Also seeing `taint key=redwood/gpu:NoSchedule` propagated inconsistently.
Ryan (oncall): Estimated customer impact? Which routes are affected?
Maya C.: Customer-impact: two higher-tier customers (realtime-infer) seeing 40-60% increased tail latency and intermittent 503s for short windows. Support already received tickets.
Alyssa S.: Quick mitigation plan: 1) Temporarily scale up a backup nodegroup with matching AMI/attachrole manually 2) Patch launch template on primary nodegroup 3) Remove problematic taint from stuck nodes so existing pods can schedule onto non-GPU pool where feasible.
Jay K.: I'll create nodegroup `gpu-ephemeral-1` with the verified launch-config and attachrole. Command I'm about to run:
```
aws autoscaling create-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name gpu-ephemeral-1 --launch-template LaunchTemplateId=lt-0abcd --min-size 0 --max-size 10 --desired-capacity 4 --tags Key=redwood:stack,Value=gpu
```
Jay K.: After instances boot, we'll label them and set taint to allow critical pod scheduling: `kubectl label node <node> node-role.kubernetes.io/gpu=ephemeral` then `kubectl taint nodes <node> redwood/gpu:NoSchedule-`
Alyssa S.: Meanwhile I'm toggling cluster-autoscaler to debug and increasing scale-up limit by +4 to allow faster handoff. Patch: `kubectl -n kube-system patch deployment cluster-autoscaler -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"cluster-autoscaler","env":[{"name":"--max-node-provision-time","value":"15m"}]}}]}}}'` (will validate first).
devops-bot: Noted scale change request. Applying cluster-autoscaler replica bump to 2.
Ryan (oncall): If we spin ephemeral nodes, we should also add a routing policy to send lower-priority customer traffic to fallback model edges to reduce queue pressure. Maya can you confirm if support can notify customers about temporary degraded latency?
Maya C.: Yes — sending status update now. Short message: "We're aware of increased latency for realtime inference in us-west-2. Engineers are actively mitigating; we expect partial restoration within ~20-30m. Will follow up when resolved."
Alyssa S.: Manual nodegroup created and instances are in provisioning. Seeing kubelet logs on one node: `E0907 12:03:21.123 kubelet.go:123] failed to register node: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` — suggests AMI missing our CA bundle. Jay, can we force bootstrap with our init script?
Jay K.: That explains boot drift. I'm launching another ephemeral node with the verified AMI id `ami-0goodami123` and attachrole `gpu-attach-role-v2`. Also patching launch template lt-0primary to point at that AMI and adding userdata fix.
Alyssa S.: Once nodes are Ready I'll remove taints from selected stuck nodes to let pods drain onto new nodes gradually: `kubectl drain <old-node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then `kubectl uncordon <old-node>` after migration.
devops-bot: New nodes registered: gpu-ephemeral-1-0, gpu-ephemeral-1-1 (Ready).
Ryan (oncall): Starting gradual traffic reroute: switching 20% of realtime-infer requests to fallback endpoints to relieve queue. Watch queues for 5m and report.
Alyssa S.: Queue decreased from ~1200 -> ~420 within 6 minutes after ephemeral nodes Ready + reroute. Error rate from realtime-infer dropped from 6.1% -> 1.4%.
Maya C.: Customers notified. Getting thumbs-up from one impacted customer that traffic looks better.
Jay K.: Primary launch template patched and pushed as new version. Scheduling a rollout to nodegroup but keeping desired capacity conservative while we verify stability. Also opened a ticket with infra -> need CI gating on AMI bake to prevent future drift.
Alyssa S.: Next steps: 1) keep ephemeral nodes for +30m as buffer 2) run full cluster-autoscaler test on staging with latest launch-template changes 3) post-incident doc + root cause analysis (likely AMI drift + attachrole timing causing register backoff and taint propagation).
Ryan (oncall): I'll take incident bridge notes and start postmortem outline. Anyone want to add action items?
Maya C.: Add: proactive customer runbook to auto-route to fallback model for severe queue spikes.
Jay K.: Add: implement CI check ensuring AMI includes CA and kubelet configs; also validate LaunchTemplate versioning automation.
Alyssa S.: Add: cluster-autoscaler hard limit alert thresholds + test harness for register timeouts.
devops-bot: Incident state -> mitigated. Current queue 120, error rate 0.5%, baseline latency returning.
Ryan (oncall): Thanks team. I'll keep bridge open for 30m to monitor, then call resolution when stable.
Maya C.: Thanks — I'll post customer follow-up once we have the RCA. :white_check_mark:
